correctness.rationale: The signed maximal cofactors form a one-dimensional null vector with no zero entries. Under independent column sign flips precisely two sign patterns make all coefficients the same sign; these patterns give a positive normalized null vector and nonzero augmented determinant, hence strict full-dimensional containment. The unsigned vector is unchanged throughout an orbit, so orbit averaging establishes its independence of E and the asserted joint conditional law without any moment or absolute-continuity assumption. On E the augmented determinant is the absolute sum of the cofactors and the normalized absolute values are barycentric coordinates. Factoring independent standard Gaussian columns into lengths and sphere directions, and using the Gram–Schmidt chi factors for the Gaussian determinant, telescopes to the stated a_d. Conditional on each prior span the mean squared successive projected length is the remaining dimension divided by d, giving d!/d^d for d columns and d!/d^{d−1} for their common d−1 columns. The missing normal projections in two minors are conditionally independent with mean absolute coordinate c_d. Inserting radial powers and counting ordered pairs gives both formulas. In d=3 a shared cross-product length has cubic mean 3π/16, with remaining axial absolute moments 1/2, 1/3 and 1/4. The three-distinct term factors into three squared projected lengths of mean 2/3 and the angular expectation: on 0<v<u<π the inner integral of sin(v)sin(u−v) is (sin u−u cos u)/2; doubling and integrating against sin u, divided by π², gives 3/(4π). Thus the three-distinct correlation is 2/(9π). The cube coefficients are 4, 36, 24; the resulting centered cubic and rational upper bound were also checked with python3 /workspace/independent_arithmetic_checks.py. Its derivative increases and is positive already at 223/71; at 22/7 the centered expression is −1091/6519744. The frozen script and requirements were read, not executed; its finite tests do not prove the identities.

value.rationale: The Euclidean volume of a random simplex containing the origin is a natural conditioned geometric invariant. The first and second formulas separate the radial and angular effects; the third determines the direction of asymmetry exactly for spherical tetrahedra, beyond a tail, an unconditioned value, or a single determinant calculation. The evaluated overlap integral makes that distinction substantive, and the joint minor representation gives an exact sampler for the volume and its barycentric marks.
